answer: **Answer:** Power BI offers a variety of visual types for data analysis. Some major types mentioned in internal documentation include correlation visuals, such as Bubble Charts, Column Lines, and Scatter Plots. Correlation visuals help determine whether two or more variables are related. The Column Line chart combines a column and line chart, with each variable having its own y-axis. The Scatterplot visual uses dots to show the relationship between variables. Distribution visuals such as Bubble Charts and Grouped Bars are used to show the frequency of values in a dataset. Additionally, in the part-to-whole category, visuals like Donut charts, Stacked Bars, and Treemaps are used to display segments as parts of a whole. Ranking visuals include Ribbon charts and Ordered Columns, which are good for showing ordered lists and stages, such as sales stages or ranking data points.
